title: Export Selected Model Names to Excel with an ARIS Report
description: Create a simple Excel list of the models you select in ARIS, using a short report script.

content.html:
Need a quick list of model names for a review or a handover? This report writes one selected model per row in an Excel workbook.

Run it on selected models

Create a report in code view with Model context and Excel output. Paste the script below, then select one or more models and run the report. These APIs run inside ARIS report scripting.

What you get

The Models worksheet contains a Model name heading followed by the selected models, using the report's selected language. Selecting two models produces two data rows. With no selected models, only the heading is written.

getSelectedModels() supplies the selection, createRow() adds each row, and write() saves the workbook. The script reads model names without changing repository content.

API reference: ARIS 10.0.27 Excel workbook API.

title: Count Function Occurrences in Selected ARIS Models
description: Export a small Excel summary showing how many function occurrences each selected model contains.

content.html:
A small count can help you compare models before a review. This report creates an Excel sheet with the model name and the number of function occurrences drawn in that model.

The report

Create a report in code view with Model context and Excel output. Select the models you want to compare and run this script inside ARIS.

Read the result

If a selected model contains five function occurrences, its row shows 5. A model with none shows 0.

ObjOccListFilter(Constants.OT_FUNC) returns occurrences whose object type is Function. If the same function definition appears twice in a model, both appearances are counted. Function occurrences drawn with other symbols, including process interfaces of that object type, are included too. This is an occurrence count, not a count of unique function definitions or a filtered activity count.

API reference: ARIS 10.0.27 Model.ObjOccListFilter(int).

title: Hide the Database Switcher in ARIS Connect
description: Simplify a classic ARIS Connect header with a three-line CSS rule that hides the database selector.

content.html:
When a portal is intended for a single database, the database selector can take up unnecessary space in the header. In classic ARIS Connect configurations that use the selectors below, a small CSS override hides it.

Add this CSS

Append the rule to a stylesheet already loaded by your active custom Connect configuration, typically under resources/css/. Creating a new CSS file alone will not load it; use your existing custom stylesheet for this example.

Check the result

Apply the updated configuration using your environment's normal deployment process and reload Connect. The database selector should disappear while the other header controls remain visible. Remove the rule to show it again.

This is a visual change only: it does not select a database or change database access permissions. The rule applies to classic Connect layouts that expose these CSS selectors. If it has no effect in your version or theme, inspect the selector in the browser and confirm that your stylesheet is loaded.

title: Change the Active Navigation Color in ARIS Connect
description: Use a small CSS override to give selected navigation items a consistent accent color in classic ARIS Connect.

content.html:
A consistent selection color makes it easier to see where you are in a portal. This example changes the border accent of selected navigation items to purple.

Add the override

Append this rule to the custom stylesheet already loaded by your active Connect configuration, typically under resources/css/. The selectors cover the navigation list and the regular or collapsible navigation bar used in this classic Connect layout.

Make it your own

Replace #7c3aed with your accent color, apply the updated configuration through your normal deployment process and reload Connect. Navigate between sections and check that the selected item's existing border uses the new color. This rule changes border color; it does not create a border where the theme has none.

!important lets this small override take priority over competing normal theme rules. These selectors are specific to the classic Connect layout used in the source example, so check them when using a different theme or ARIS version.
